title: Tenant microburst capacitor for console ingress smoothing and adaptive watermarking
creator: Sana Patel
description:
Background: Console ingestion occasionally sees short-lived but intense microbursts from some tenants (CI pipelines, SDK retries, or misconfigured clients) that spike ingress queues and cause 99th percentile latency degradations for other tenants. Existing admission control is per-tenant coarse-grained throttling and global reservoir-based shedding which either allows noisy neighbors to impact tail latency or over-throttles long-running tenants.

Goal: Implement a tenant-aware microburst capacitor that smooths short bursts (sub-second to few-second) while preserving steady-state throughput and respecting per-tenant SLAs. The capacitor should provide: (1) low-jitter smoothing for short bursts, (2) bounded buffer memory per tenant and graceful spillover to elastic lanes, (3) adaptive watermarking to control replay and late-arrival handling, and (4) observability hooks for per-tenant queue depth, smoothing latency, and spillover rates.

Design summary: The capacitor is an ingress component that sits between the edge gateway and the main intake queue. Key elements:
- Per-tenant median-rate estimator (sliding window 30s with exponential decay) to compute expected baseline rate.
- Short-term token-bucket overlay (burst window 250–2000ms): allows controlled bursts above baseline up to a configurable burst allowance.
- Hysteretic admission window: when ingress latency crosses threshold (configurable by route / plan), the capacitor tightens refill rates for tenants showing repeated microbursts.
- Elastic spillover lanes: overflow events for a tenant are redirected to a best-effort spillover pool (lower priority, configurable TTL) that still persists events for downstream replay if capacity frees.
- Adaptive watermarking: each tenant stream maintains a watermark that determines which events are treated as on-time vs late-arrival; watermarks are adjusted by observed event-time skew and slot occupancy to avoid unnecessary reordering and replay storms.

Implementation notes:
- Stateless control plane with per-tenant ephemeral state stored in a compact in-memory structure (capped by LRU) and periodically snapshotted to Redis for fast warm-start.
- Admission logic implemented in Rust as an independent microservice (ingress-capacitor) exposing a gRPC control API and an Envoy filter for placement.
- Backpressure signaling uses x-envoy-backend-retry-after header + Delta-encoded lease token when rejections are temporary.
- Metrics: per-tenant queue_depth, smoothing_delay_p50/p95/p99, burst_reject_rate, spillover_count, watermark_lag.

Trade-offs considered:
- Memory vs accuracy: we limit per-tenant state to first N active tenants and approximate long-tail tenants via a shared reservoir to bound memory.
- Latency vs loss: we prefer temporary spillover over immediate drop to avoid user-visible data loss; however heavy sustained overload will trigger shedding with prioritized tenants preserved.
- Complexity vs observability: watermark adaptation adds complexity but reduces replay storms; we will instrument thoroughly and provide toggles for early rollback.

Acceptance criteria:
- On synthetic microburst test (200ms bursts at 5x baseline for 100 tenants), smoothing_delay_p99 < 250ms and overall 99th ingestion latency reduced by at least 40% compared to current baseline.
- No increase in per-tenant steady-state tail latency beyond 5% for tenants not exhibiting bursts.
- Spillover pool end-to-end delivery success >= 95% within 60s under burst conditions.
- Feature rollout with canary on "beta" organization and automated rollback if drop rate > 0.5% for priority tenants.

Docs and artifacts: design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/TC-2026/microburst-capacitor-design, implementation RFC: /docs/ingest/ingress-capacitor-rfc.md, spike notebook with load tests: gs://redwood-loadtests/microburst-capacitor/2026-02-28.

Notes for rollout: start with tenant whitelisting (beta customers), enable observability retention 7d, run side-by-side in pass-through mode for 48h to collect baselines, then enable smoothing flags for canary group, followed by gradual ramp to 20% of orgs, measure metrics, then full rollout if acceptance criteria pass.

comments: 2026-02-22 - Sana Patel: Initial spike validated using the SDK harness. Observed 3x 99th latency explosion for non-burst tenants during tenant A simulated retries. Attached load logs.
2026-02-26 - Miguel Ortega: Prototype token-bucket overlay implemented (`cap-rt/ingress_capacitor` branch). Needs integration tests for watermark logic.
2026-03-03 - Jon Huang (SRE): Concerned about Redis snapshot frequency; recommended reducing snapshot interval to 5s for faster recovery. Added as follow-up task.
2026-03-05 - Design review (Katherine Li): Approved overall approach; requested clearer UX for tenant admins to view spillover state and TTLs in Console.

2026-03-09 - QA (Anita Gomez): Running chaos tests injecting clock skew and late-arrival events. Observed one replay storm when watermark adaptation was too aggressive; mitigation implemented by clamping watermark delta per minute.

2026-03-12 - Miguel Ortega: Implemented spillover lane with S3-backed buffer for best-effort events (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/842). Integration tests passing in staging. Preparing canary manifest.
notes: Plan: land capacitor in staging behind feature flag, run 72h canary with metric windows and automated rollback hooks. Next: add RBAC visibility in Console and add per-tenant admin controls (max_burst, spillover_ttl).
